findings.finding: ik_usec covers all of _apply_pose: skeleton changes, static/swept target queries, self/world tests and holder recovery. It is not pure arm IK and must not be added to its nested static/sweep/world timings.

Conditional exact duplicate: early safe-bones fallback restores clav/upper/fore/hand; the IK loop changes upper/fore/hand only; final safe-bones fallback restores the same saved poses again. With unchanged holder/rig ancestors/target/channel, its transform and rejection may repeat exactly.
findings.support: spear_contact_resume29.gd:43-51 records both arms clav/upper/fore/hand. sword_prototype.gd:3496-3556 and3573-3581 only set upper/fore/hand in this invocation.
findings.safe_plan: Instrument candidate label, exact transform equality and target/channel/holder state. Only if proved identical, reuse the earlier negative result within this one _apply_pose call, while still restoring the actual bones. Preserve obstruction data. Never reuse an accepted result; never carry results between frames or dispatches.
findings.risk: Same weapon transform alone is insufficient for self collision; current rig/body state matters. query_static also orients its response normal using holder position. Restore metadata consistently. At most one candidate rejection is removed by this narrow shortcut; it is not a demonstrated cure for180ms.

findings.finding: Most expensive attempts are not duplicates: 5/28 IK attempts change origin/axis, then recovery tries7 distances and up to8 different directions. findings.safe_plan: Measure branch-specific call counts and exact duplicate transforms before considering exact direction deduplication. Do not quantize positions, normals, geometry or channel keys; narrow bores make approximate reuse unsafe.
